ColonyCouncil.ArcDef.label: bad nights
ColonyCouncil.ArcDef.summary: A child with nightmares, or a fright that won't let go, and a parent or a grown-up fond of them who sits up with them until the nights are quiet again.

li.label: bad nights
li.waiting: Next: {OTHER_nameDef} sits up with {PAWN_nameDef} after a bad dream.

plain.li: I had the bad dream again. The one with the door. I didn't tell anyone because they'd say it's only a dream.
[nightmare] I woke up and couldn't remember where I was, and then I could, and that was worse for a bit.
[fear] I don't like the dark since the fighting. I pretend I'm asleep so nobody knows I'm not.
I keep my eyes open as long as I can so the dream can't get in. It gets in anyway.

warm.li: I don't want to wake anybody up. Everybody works so hard. I hold the blanket over my mouth so I don't make any noise.

blunt.li: Bad dream. Again. I hate it.

cheerful.li: I had a scary dream but I'm brave, mostly. I only cried a bit, and then I counted the roof beams.

gloomy.li: The bad dream always comes back. It's going to come back tonight.

cold.li: I have had the same nightmare four times. I am counting them.

plain.li: {OTHER_nameDef} has dark rings under {OTHER_possessive} eyes and jumps at loud noises. Something's frightening that child at night.
Heard {OTHER_nameDef} crying in the night and went to look. {OTHER_nameDef} pretended to be asleep. I know that trick. I used it at that age.

warm.li: {OTHER_nameDef} isn't sleeping. I'm going to sit up with {OTHER_objective} tonight, whatever the work in the morning.

chronicle.li: Someone has been crying at night and pretending to be asleep when anyone comes to look. It's {PAWN_nameDef}, and {OTHER_nameDef} has noticed.
Nightmares have been keeping young {PAWN_nameDef} awake.

li.label: a light by the bed
li.waiting: Next: some good days, or a better dream.

plain.li: {OTHER_nameDef} sat up with me and we checked under the bed and behind the door. Nothing there. {OTHER_nameDef} left a candle burning.
{OTHER_nameDef} said everybody has bad dreams, even grown-ups. Even {OTHER_nameDef}. I didn't know that.
{OTHER_nameDef} told me a story about a brave mouse until I fell asleep. I didn't hear the end. I'll ask tomorrow.

warm.li: {OTHER_nameDef} stayed until I was asleep. When I woke up {OTHER_nameDef} was asleep in the chair. I put my blanket on {OTHER_objective}.

blunt.li: {OTHER_nameDef} stayed up with me. The dream didn't come. Good.

cheerful.li: I have my own lamp now, for nights! It's the best thing I own.

gloomy.li: {OTHER_nameDef} was nice to me, but {OTHER_nameDef} can't stay up every night. The dream knows that.

cold.li: With a light burning and {OTHER_nameDef} near, the nightmare did not come. I will repeat the experiment.

plain.li: Sat up with {OTHER_nameDef} until the shaking stopped. We made up a story about a mouse who wasn't afraid of anything. It was a long story.

chronicle.li: {OTHER_nameDef} sat up with {PAWN_nameDef}, checked under the bed and behind the door, and left a light burning.

plain.li: I slept all night. All of it. I didn't even remember to be scared.
The dark is just the dark. {OTHER_nameDef} said it would be, and it is.
I had a dream about flying instead. I want that one again.

warm.li: I'm not scared at night now. If anyone else gets bad dreams, I'll sit up with them, like {OTHER_nameDef} did.

blunt.li: No more bad dreams. Done with those.

cheerful.li: I slept the whole night and woke up starving! I ate two breakfasts.

gloomy.li: The bad dream hasn't come for a while. I'm keeping the light, just in case.

cold.li: The nightmares have stopped. I have kept a record. It ends here.

plain.li: {OTHER_nameDef} slept the whole night through and came to breakfast hungry. I didn't realize how worried I'd been until it stopped.

chronicle.li: {PAWN_nameDef} sleeps through the night again, and {OTHER_nameDef} has gone back to {OTHER_possessive} own bed.
Young {PAWN_nameDef} sleeps through the night again.

plain.li: [otherdead] {OTHER_nameDef} used to sit up with me when the bad dreams came. Now the chair is empty.
[otherleft] {OTHER_nameDef} is gone. I keep the light on by myself now.
[timeout] The bad dreams still come sometimes. I've got used to them, which isn't the same as them going away.
I still have bad nights. Not every night. Some.

gloomy.li: [otherdead] Now I have a new bad dream, and it's about {OTHER_nameDef}.

fizzleChronicle.li: [otherdead] {OTHER_nameDef} died, and {PAWN_nameDef}'s bad nights came back.
{PAWN_nameDef} still has bad nights now and then.

plain.li: {OTHER_nameDef} was only small, and so frightened of the dark. I sat up with {OTHER_objective}. I'd sit up every night for the rest of my life to have that back.
{OTHER_nameDef}'s light is still by the bed. None of us can bring ourselves to put it out.

cold.li: {OTHER_nameDef} was a child. There is nothing else to say that would help.

ColonyCouncil.ArcDef.label: not a child any more
ColonyCouncil.ArcDef.summary: A young person (13 to 19) at odds with a parent or an older colonist who still treats them like a child sets out to prove otherwise in the work they love, until the two of them can talk as equals.

li.label: treated like a child
li.waiting: Next: hard work at {SKILL}, enough to be noticed.

plain.li: {OTHER_nameDef} checked my work again today, out loud, at the bench, like I'm still small. I'm not small.
Every time I have an idea, {OTHER_nameDef} says "when you're older". I am older. I'm older every single day.
I'll show {OTHER_nameDef}. I'll get so good at {SKILL} that nobody can say anything.
[kin] My own parent still treats me like I'm five. {OTHER_nameDef} doesn't see me at all, just who I used to be.

warm.li: I know {OTHER_nameDef} only wants to keep me safe. I just wish {OTHER_pronoun} could see I can keep myself safe now.

blunt.li: {OTHER_nameDef} thinks I'm a child. Wrong.

cheerful.li: I'm going to be the best at {SKILL} in the whole colony, and then {OTHER_nameDef} will have to listen to me!

gloomy.li: Nothing I do will ever be enough for {OTHER_nameDef}. I'm doing it anyway.

cold.li: {OTHER_nameDef} underestimates me. I will provide evidence to the contrary.

plain.li: {OTHER_nameDef} sulked all day because I checked {OTHER_possessive} work. Someone has to check it. {OTHER_nameDef} is still young.

blunt.li: {OTHER_nameDef} wants to be treated like a grown-up. Then {OTHER_nameDef} can act like one.

chronicle.li: "When you're older," {OTHER_nameDef} keeps telling {PAWN_nameDef}. {PAWN_nameDef} has decided not to wait.
Young {PAWN_nameDef} has been throwing {PAWN_objective}self into {SKILL}, to show {OTHER_nameDef} a thing or two.

li.label: proving it
li.waiting: Next: a real talk with {OTHER_nameDef}, as equals.

plain.li: I've been working at {SKILL} every hour I'm allowed and some I'm not. People have started to notice. One of them is {OTHER_nameDef}.
{OTHER_nameDef} looked at my work today and didn't say anything at all. That's new.

warm.li: I think {OTHER_nameDef} is proud of me and doesn't know how to say it. I'm going to help {OTHER_objective} say it.

blunt.li: I'm good at {SKILL} now. Everyone can see it.

cheerful.li: Somebody asked ME for help with {SKILL} today. A grown-up!

gloomy.li: I've worked so hard. {OTHER_nameDef} still hasn't said anything. Maybe {OTHER_pronoun} never will.

cold.li: My work is good now, and {OTHER_nameDef} knows it. I'm waiting for {OTHER_objective} to say so.

chronicle.li: {OTHER_nameDef} looked over {PAWN_nameDef}'s work in {SKILL} today and found nothing to correct.

li.label: a grown-up's word
li.waiting: Next: some days of {PAWN_nameDef} and {OTHER_nameDef} getting on.

plain.li: {OTHER_nameDef} and I argued about the work, and for once it was an argument, not a telling-off. I won some of it.
{OTHER_nameDef} asked my opinion. Then listened to it. I didn't know what to do with my face.

warm.li: {OTHER_nameDef} said sorry for treating me like a child. I said sorry for acting like one. We both laughed.

blunt.li: {OTHER_nameDef} talked to me like a grown-up. About time.

cheerful.li: {OTHER_nameDef} and I had a proper talk, like two people. I'm walking about a foot taller.

gloomy.li: {OTHER_nameDef} talked to me properly today. Tomorrow {OTHER_pronoun}'ll probably check my work again anyway.

cold.li: {OTHER_nameDef} has revised {OTHER_possessive} estimate of me. The conversation was overdue.

plain.li: Talked with {OTHER_nameDef} today and realized halfway through I was talking to a grown person. When did that happen?

chronicle.li: {OTHER_nameDef} asked {PAWN_nameDef}'s opinion, and then listened to the answer.

plain.li: Nobody's said "when you're older" to me in weeks. I think I just am older now.
{OTHER_nameDef} asked me to take charge of a job today. In charge. Of a job. With grown-ups on it.
[kin] My parent introduced me to a trader as "my {SKILL} expert". I nearly fell over.

warm.li: {OTHER_nameDef} and I are friends now, I think. That's better than being proved right.

blunt.li: They treat me like a grown-up now. Good. I am one.

cheerful.li: I'm grown! Not officially. But they've stopped checking my work.

gloomy.li: Being treated like a grown-up means grown-up work. I'm not sure I wanted it this much.

cold.li: My standing in the colony has changed. I intend to deserve it.

plain.li: I put {OTHER_nameDef} in charge of a job today. {OTHER_nameDef} did it better than I would have. I'll never say so. I just did, here.

chronicle.li: {PAWN_nameDef} is taken for grown now, by {OTHER_nameDef} as much as anyone.
{OTHER_nameDef} has stopped treating {PAWN_nameDef} like a child.

plain.li: [fight] {OTHER_nameDef} and I had it out with fists. I'm not proud of it. I'm not sorry either.
[otherdead] {OTHER_nameDef} is dead, and I never got to show {OTHER_objective} what I could do.
[otherleft] {OTHER_nameDef} is gone. I'm still trying to prove something to someone who isn't here.
[timeout] Whatever I do, {OTHER_nameDef} still sees a child. I'm done trying.
I'm still the child in {OTHER_nameDef}'s eyes. Maybe I always will be.

blunt.li: [timeout] Fine. Let {OTHER_nameDef} think what {OTHER_pronoun} likes.

gloomy.li: [timeout] I knew it. I'll always be the child who knocked the pot over.

fizzleChronicle.li: [fight] {PAWN_nameDef} and {OTHER_nameDef} came to blows, and nothing was proved.

plain.li: {OTHER_nameDef} was so close to grown. I treated {OTHER_objective} like a child, and now I'll never get to treat {OTHER_objective} like anything else.
{OTHER_nameDef} wanted so badly to be taken seriously. I take {OTHER_objective} seriously now. Too late.

cold.li: {OTHER_nameDef} died young, before any of us had got round to taking {OTHER_objective} seriously.

ColonyCouncil.ArcDef.label: a new parent
ColonyCouncil.ArcDef.summary: A baby of theirs born in the colony: sleepless nights, a pair of hands from someone who cares, and finding their feet as a parent.

li.label: no sleep
li.waiting: Next: a few days, if {PAWN_nameDef} can stay awake for them.

plain.li: {NAME} is here. Small, loud, perfect. I haven't slept since. I may never sleep again.
I held {NAME} all morning and forgot to eat. Forgot I had work. Someone had to come and find me.
[night] {NAME} cried for three hours. I walked up and down until the floorboards learned my name.

warm.li: I look at {NAME} and want to be a better person, immediately, today. I'm too tired for most of it.

blunt.li: Baby. No sleep. Send help.

cheerful.li: {NAME} smiled at me! Everyone says it's wind. It wasn't wind.

gloomy.li: {NAME} is so small. Everything out there is so big. I don't know how anyone does this.

cold.li: {NAME} requires attention every two hours. I have revised all my other commitments.

chronicle.li: {PAWN_nameDef} is a new parent, and the colony can tell by the dark rings under {PAWN_possessive} eyes.
Little {NAME} has arrived, and {PAWN_nameDef} hasn't slept since.

li.label: a pair of hands
li.waiting: Next: someone takes the baby for a while.

plain.li: I fell asleep standing up at the workbench. Someone has to take {NAME} for a few hours or I'll drop.
Plenty of advice going round. Not one offer to walk {NAME} up and down at three in the morning.

warm.li: I don't like asking for help. I'm going to have to learn.

blunt.li: Need sleep. Need someone to hold {NAME}. Anyone.

cheerful.li: {NAME} has the loudest voice in the colony. I've never been so proud of a noise.

gloomy.li: I'm doing it all wrong. {NAME} cries and I can't make it stop.

cold.li: I've slept four hours in three days and I'm making mistakes at work. That has to be fixed before it costs someone.

chronicle.li: {PAWN_nameDef} fell asleep on {PAWN_possessive} feet at work today. Someone needs to take little {NAME} for a night.

li.label: finding our feet
li.waiting: Next: some good days, for {PAWN_nameDef} and {NAME} both.

plain.li: {OTHER_nameDef} took {NAME} for the whole night and I slept eleven hours. I woke up and cried, from gratitude, mostly.
{OTHER_nameDef} walked {NAME} up and down while I ate a hot meal, sitting down. I'd forgotten that was possible.

warm.li: {OTHER_nameDef} has been so kind to {NAME} and me. We're going to be all right with friends like that.

blunt.li: {OTHER_nameDef} took the baby. I slept. Saved my life.

cheerful.li: {OTHER_nameDef} sang {NAME} to sleep! I'm learning the song.

gloomy.li: {OTHER_nameDef} helped. I should be able to do this myself.

cold.li: {OTHER_nameDef} took the night. I owe {OTHER_objective} one, and I'll pay it.

chronicle.li: {OTHER_nameDef} walked little {NAME} up and down until dawn so that {PAWN_nameDef} could sleep.

plain.li: {NAME} slept most of the night, and so did I. I think we've worked each other out.
I know which cry means hungry and which means bored and which means pick me up. I'm a parent. When did that happen?
Carried {NAME} round the colony this evening and introduced {NAME} to everything. The well was a great success.

warm.li: I'm going to give {NAME} the best of everything I have, and I have more than I thought.

blunt.li: Baby's sleeping. I'm sleeping. We'll manage.

cheerful.li: {NAME} and I have a routine now. It falls apart every day at noon, but it's ours.

gloomy.li: We're doing all right. I still get up twice a night to listen to the baby breathe.

cold.li: {NAME} and I have a routine that works. I didn't expect to like it this much.

chronicle.li: {PAWN_nameDef} has found {PAWN_possessive} feet as a parent, and little {NAME} is thriving.

plain.li: [babygone] There are no words for this. I'm not going to write any.
[timeout] Still tired. Still a parent. Still learning.
I'm getting through the days with {NAME}. That will have to do.

cold.li: [babygone] I will not write about this.

fizzleChronicle.li: {PAWN_nameDef} is still finding {PAWN_possessive} way as a parent.

plain.li: {OTHER_nameDef} had a baby who needed {OTHER_objective}. We'll make sure {NAME} knows who {OTHER_nameDef} was.
{OTHER_nameDef} was a new parent, tired and happy. I'll help raise {NAME}. I promised myself at the grave.

cold.li: {OTHER_nameDef} leaves a child behind. The colony will have to be enough of a family.

ColonyCouncil.ArcDef.label: one more spring
ColonyCouncil.ArcDef.summary: Someone old (65 or more) whose body has started to fail puts their affairs in order: what they want done told to someone they trust, one last piece of work, and peace.

li.label: the body tells
li.waiting: Next: a few days to think it over.

plain.li: My body has started sending me messages. Short ones, mostly in the mornings. I've decided to listen.
It took me three tries to get out of bed today. I'm not frightened. I'm taking notes.
[winter] The cold gets into my bones now and stays. I'd like to see one more spring, and I'd like my affairs in order before it.

warm.li: I've had a long life and a good one, mostly. I'd like to leave things tidy for the people I love.

blunt.li: Getting old. Body's quitting on me. Time to sort things out.

cheerful.li: I creak like an old door now. A good door, mind, with a lot of stories behind it.

gloomy.li: So this is how it starts. A stair at a time. I'll do what I can while I can.

cold.li: My health is declining. I intend to make arrangements while I am still able to.

chronicle.li: {PAWN_nameDef} has been slow on the stairs lately, and slower in the mornings, and has started to think about what comes after.
{PAWN_nameDef} has begun to put {PAWN_possessive} affairs in order, without any fuss.

li.label: putting things in order
li.waiting: Next: {PAWN_nameDef} tells someone they trust what they want done.

plain.li: I've made a list of my things and who should have them. It was a short list and a long afternoon.
There's a spot by the graves with a good view of the fields. I'd like that one, when the time comes. Somebody should know.

warm.li: I want to tell {OTHER_nameDef} what I'd like done. Not to make {OTHER_objective} sad. So it's one less thing for {OTHER_objective} to wonder.

blunt.li: Got to tell someone what I want. Probably {OTHER_nameDef}.

cheerful.li: I've picked out my spot by the graves! It has a lovely view. I'll be very comfortable.

gloomy.li: Somebody has to know what I want before I can't say it. I keep putting it off.

cold.li: My instructions need a keeper. {OTHER_nameDef} is reliable.

chronicle.li: {PAWN_nameDef} has made a list of who gets the good knife, who gets the coat, and who gets the chair by the door.

li.label: a look at the spot by the graves
one last piece
li.waiting: Next: one last good piece of work in {SKILL}.

plain.li: Told {OTHER_nameDef} everything. {OTHER_nameDef} listened, didn't argue, and wrote it down. I knew I'd picked right.
Now that's done, I want to make one more thing in {SKILL}. Something to leave behind that isn't a list.

warm.li: {OTHER_nameDef} held my hand while I talked. I'm going to make something for the colony now, while my hands still do what I tell them.

blunt.li: Told {OTHER_nameDef}. Done. One more job and then I rest.

cheerful.li: One last masterpiece! Well, one last piece. We'll see about the master part.

gloomy.li: My hands shake now. I'm going to make one more thing anyway.

cold.li: My wishes are written down. One job left, and I won't hand it to anyone else.

plain.li: {OTHER_nameDef} told me what {OTHER_pronoun} wants done when the time comes. I wrote it all down. I'll keep it safe, and I hope I won't need it for a long while.

chronicle.li: "Write it down," {PAWN_nameDef} told {OTHER_nameDef}, and {OTHER_nameDef} did. Then {PAWN_nameDef} went off to make one last good thing.

plain.li: Finished it. It's not my best work. It's my last good work, and that's a different thing, and better.
I've done what I meant to do. Now I'm going to sit in the sun and let the young ones run things badly.

warm.li: The work's done and the people I love know what I want. There's nothing left but to enjoy the days.

blunt.li: Work's done. Sitting down now.

cheerful.li: Done! Now I'm going to be a terrible nuisance and give everyone advice.

gloomy.li: It's finished. I don't quite know what to do with my hands.

cold.li: The last job's done. I have nothing to do and no one waiting on me, and I don't mind it.

chronicle.li: {PAWN_nameDef}'s last work in {SKILL} is done, and {PAWN_pronoun} has carried a chair out into the sun.

plain.li: My affairs are in order and I'm in no hurry. If I get one more spring, I'll spend it well.
The children have started asking me for stories. I've got a lot of them. I'd better get on.
I'm ready for whatever comes, and I'm not waiting for it. There's a lot of sitting in the sun still to do.

warm.li: I'm at peace. The people here will look after each other. That's all I ever wanted to know.

blunt.li: Everything's sorted. I'm content. Leave me be.

cheerful.li: I've never felt better about feeling worse! I've started planting a tree I'll never sit under. I'm enjoying the digging.

gloomy.li: I've made my peace. Some days that's a comfort. Most days, actually.

cold.li: Everything I can do is done. The rest isn't my concern.

chronicle.li: {PAWN_nameDef} has put {PAWN_possessive} affairs in order and is at peace, and in no hurry.
Old {PAWN_nameDef} is ready for whatever comes, and spends the days in the sun with the children's questions.

plain.li: [timeout] I meant to get everything in order. There's always one more thing. I'll get to it.
My affairs are mostly in order. Mostly will have to do.

blunt.li: [timeout] Didn't finish sorting things. Someone else can.

fizzleChronicle.li: {PAWN_nameDef} never quite finished putting {PAWN_possessive} affairs in order.

plain.li: {OTHER_nameDef} told me exactly what {OTHER_pronoun} wanted, down to the spot by the graves with the view of the fields. I've seen to all of it.
{OTHER_nameDef} was putting things in order to the very end. {OTHER_nameDef} would hate how untidy we all are about the grief.
{OTHER_nameDef} wanted one more spring. It's coming. I'll plant something by the grave.

cold.li: {OTHER_nameDef} had made arrangements. They are being carried out exactly.

ColonyCouncil.ArcDef.label: the last two of us
ColonyCouncil.ArcDef.summary: Two old colonists (55 or more) who have long been at odds find they are the last who remember the old days, and slowly stop being at odds.

li.label: two old goats
li.waiting: Next: some hours near {OTHER_nameDef}, not fighting.

plain.li: {OTHER_nameDef} sat in my chair in the sun again. My chair. We've been doing this for years.
{OTHER_nameDef} told one of the young ones that I've been wrong about the harvest every year since we came. I have not. Most years.
Looked round the table tonight and counted. {OTHER_nameDef} and I are the only ones left from the early days. Of all the people.

warm.li: {OTHER_nameDef} and I have never got on. I'm too old to remember exactly why.

blunt.li: {OTHER_nameDef} is a stubborn old fool. So am I. That's the trouble.

cheerful.li: {OTHER_nameDef} and I had our usual argument about the weather. It's the most reliable thing in the colony.

gloomy.li: Everyone who knew me when I was young is gone, except {OTHER_nameDef}. It would be.

cold.li: {OTHER_nameDef} and I have been at odds for longer than some colonists have been alive. It has become habit more than conviction.

plain.li: {OTHER_nameDef} glared at me across the yard again. I glared back. Some things never change, and I'm glad of it, almost.

chronicle.li: {OTHER_nameDef} has taken {PAWN_nameDef}'s chair in the sun again. The two oldest hands in the colony have been at odds for years.

li.label: the old days
li.waiting: Next: a talk about the old days.

plain.li: {OTHER_nameDef} and I ended up on the same bench in the sun today. Neither of us would move. We sat there all afternoon, out of spite, and then it was pleasant.
One of the young ones asked about the first winter, and {OTHER_nameDef} and I answered at the same time, and both got it wrong in the same place.

warm.li: {OTHER_nameDef} remembers the same things I do. The young ones weren't there. That's worth something.

blunt.li: Sat near {OTHER_nameDef} all day. Didn't kill each other. Progress.

cheerful.li: {OTHER_nameDef} laughed at one of my jokes! By accident, but it counts.

gloomy.li: Sat with {OTHER_nameDef}. We were both thinking about the ones who are gone.

cold.li: {OTHER_nameDef} and I shared a bench without incident. Noted.

chronicle.li: Neither would give up the bench in the sun, so {PAWN_nameDef} and {OTHER_nameDef} shared it all afternoon, without a word.

li.label: a truce of sorts
li.waiting: Next: some days of {PAWN_nameDef} and {OTHER_nameDef} getting on.

plain.li: {OTHER_nameDef} and I talked about the old days until supper went cold. Neither of us could remember what we fell out about.
We named everyone who was here at the start, {OTHER_nameDef} and I. It took a long time. We were the only two left at the end of the list.

warm.li: {OTHER_nameDef} and I have been fools for years, and I think we both know it now.

blunt.li: Talked to {OTHER_nameDef}. {OTHER_nameDef}'s all right, it seems.

cheerful.li: {OTHER_nameDef} and I told the young ones the story of the first winter, together, with sound effects.

gloomy.li: {OTHER_nameDef} and I wasted so many years. There aren't many left to make up for it.

cold.li: The original cause of our dispute could not be established. It has been set aside.

chronicle.li: {PAWN_nameDef} and {OTHER_nameDef} talked about the old days, and couldn't remember what they'd fallen out about.

plain.li: {OTHER_nameDef} saved me the chair in the sun today. My chair. I let {OTHER_objective} keep it and we shared the bench.
The last two of us. We might as well be friends. I think we were, under all the glaring.
{OTHER_nameDef} and I are teaching the young ones the old songs. We still can't agree on the words of the second verse.

warm.li: {OTHER_nameDef} is my oldest friend. It took us long enough to notice.

blunt.li: {OTHER_nameDef}'s my friend now. Don't make a fuss about it.

cheerful.li: {OTHER_nameDef} and I are the colony's grumpiest double act. The children follow us about to hear us bicker.

gloomy.li: Friends at last, {OTHER_nameDef} and I. I only wish we had more years to spend on it.

cold.li: {OTHER_nameDef} and I have agreed that our rivalry was a poor use of what time we have left. We are friends now.

plain.li: {OTHER_nameDef} and I sat up talking about everyone we've buried. Then about everyone we haven't, yet. We're the last two. I'm glad it's us.

chronicle.li: {PAWN_nameDef} and {OTHER_nameDef}, the last two of the old days, are friends at last.
The colony's two oldest hands have stopped feuding and started reminiscing.

plain.li: [fight] {OTHER_nameDef} and I came to blows. At our age. Neither of us could lift our arms afterwards.
[otherdead] {OTHER_nameDef} is dead. The last one who remembered the old days with me. Now it's only me.
[otherleft] {OTHER_nameDef} has gone. There's no one left to argue about the first winter with.
[timeout] {OTHER_nameDef} and I went back to glaring at each other. Old habits.
{OTHER_nameDef} and I never quite made it up. There's still time, I tell myself.

gloomy.li: [otherdead] I'm the last one now. I spent our last years fighting with {OTHER_nameDef}.

fizzleChronicle.li: [otherdead] {OTHER_nameDef} died before {PAWN_nameDef} and {OTHER_objective} had fully made their peace.
[fight] {PAWN_nameDef} and {OTHER_nameDef} came to blows, old as they are.

plain.li: {OTHER_nameDef} and I fought for years, and we'd only just stopped. I'm the last one who remembers the old days now.
{OTHER_nameDef} always stole my chair in the sun. I'd give the chair to have {OTHER_objective} back in it.

cold.li: {OTHER_nameDef} was the last of the original settlers besides me. The colony's memory is shorter now.
